newsitem.title: USA: US high-grade corp bonds take new issue spotlight.
newsitem.headline: US high-grade corp bonds take new issue spotlight.

text.p: Investment-grade issues are expected to take the spotlight in the U.S. corporate bond market Wednesday as high-yield bond issuance takes a breather, according to syndicate officials.
Topping the action today is a $2.75 billion taxable municipal bond offering from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority via a Merrill Lynch-led syndicate.
The deal, which will consist in large part of zero coupon bonds, is expected to attract considerable interest from corporate bond investors.

A recent addition to the forward calendar is a Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp $200 million 10-year bond offering via Morgan Stanley & Co. The deal may come as early as today, sources said. Price talk on the deal, rated A2/A-minus, is around 65 basis points over Treasuries, they said.
Also expected today is a Norcen Energy Resources $250 million offering of five-year notes via Goldman Sachs.
British Aerospace Plc may bring a $600 million offering of 10-year, 30-year and 100-year bonds via J.P. Morgan Securities today as well.

Finally, Wisconsin Power and Light, a unit of WPL Holdings Inc, is expected to sell $105 million of 10-year AA3/AA-minus debentures via Merrill Lynch. Price talk is around 57 basis points over Treasuries.
The utility's ratings are watchlisted for downgrade pending a merger. As a result, the bonds are priced in the mid-single-A category, sources close to the deal said.

This morning, Sears Roebuck Acceptance Corp priced a global offering of $500 million in 10-year bonds via Goldman Sachs & Co. The deal, rated A2/A-minus, priced at a spread of 62.5 basis point spread over Treasuries.

In the high-yield bond market, Ocean Energy Inc, plans to sell $200 million in 144A senior subordinated notes via Merrill Lynch on Wednesday. Price talk on the B3/B-minus-rated deal is around 225 basis points over Treasuries.
Proceeds from the offering will be used primarily to refinance outstanding debt. Ocean Energy is an oil and gas exploration and production company based in Baton Rouge, La.

Two junk bond issues were also priced early on Wednesday: Talton Holding Inc's $115 million offering of 10-year senior notes and Sinclair Broadcast Group's $200 million offering of senior subordinated notes.
Talton's offering, rated B2/B, priced to yield 11 percent while Sinclair Broadcasting's deal, which had the same rating, priced to yield 9.40 percent.
Market sources said the yield differential is attributable to the fact that the company's are in totally seperate industries.
Talton provides phone services to prison inmates while Sinclair Broadcasting owns and operates television stations.
